questions.title: Where to put the object for a virtual image
questions.text: Rays from the sun converge at a point 25 cm behind a convex lens. The distance at which an object should be placed in front of the lens to get a virtual image is:
steps: ① Sun's rays are parallel ⟹ they meet at the focus
③ A convex lens gives a virtual image only when the object is inside F
④ Object distance < 25 cm ⟹ only 20 cm fits
questions.remember: Convex lens: object between F and the optical centre ⟹ virtual, erect, magnified image (a magnifying glass).
questions.trap: Picking 50 cm (that's 2F, giving a real, same-size image). Virtual needs the object INSIDE F.
questions.tryit: Where should the object be for a real image of the same size?

questions.title: Negative magnification greater than 1
questions.text: From the following options, choose the one which gives negative magnification greater than one:
opts: Concave mirror; nature of image: real
Concave mirror; nature of image: virtual
Convex mirror; nature of image: real
Convex mirror; nature of image: virtual
steps: ① Negative m ⟹ inverted image ⟹ REAL
③ A convex mirror never forms a real image ✗
④ Concave mirror, object between F and C ⟹ real, inverted, enlarged ✓
questions.ans: Option (a) Concave mirror; nature of image: real
questions.remember: Sign of m: negative ⟹ real and inverted; positive ⟹ virtual and erect. |m| > 1 ⟹ magnified.
questions.trap: Picking (b): a virtual image always has POSITIVE magnification.
questions.tryit: What is the sign of m for a convex mirror's image?

questions.title: Refractive index and the speed of light
questions.text:
(a) Define absolute refractive index of an optical medium.
(b) Refractive indices: A 1.50, B 1.46, C 1.31, D 1.77. Arrange these media in increasing order of speed of light through them.
steps: ① (a) n = speed of light in vacuum / speed in the medium = c/v
② (b) v = c/n ⟹ bigger n, SLOWER light
③ Slowest: D (1.77), then A (1.50), B (1.46), fastest C (1.31)
∴ Increasing speed: D < A < B < C
questions.ans: (a) Absolute refractive index n = c/v (speed of light in vacuum ÷ speed in the medium) · (b) D < A < B < C
questions.remember: n = c/v. Optically denser medium = higher n = slower light. Diamond (2.42) is among the densest.
questions.trap: Sorting by n from small to large: that's DECREASING speed. Increasing speed means largest n first.
questions.tryit: Light travels from medium C to D. Does it bend towards or away from the normal?
questions.tryans: Towards the normal (C to a denser medium D)

questions.title: Convex lens: object at 2F
questions.text: An object is placed at a distance of 30 cm in front of a convex lens of focal length 15 cm. Use the lens formula to determine the position of the image. What will be the size of the image in this case?
steps: ∴ Image 30 cm behind the lens: real, inverted, SAME size
questions.ans: v = +30 cm (on the other side, at 2F); m = −1: real, inverted, same size as the object
questions.remember: Convex lens with the object at 2F always gives the image at 2F: real, inverted, same size (m = −1).
questions.trap: Writing u = +30. The object is in front of the lens, against the light: u is NEGATIVE.
questions.tryit: If the object moves to 20 cm, where is the image?

questions.title: Concave lens: image distance and height
steps: ① u = −30 cm, f = −15 cm (concave), h = 6 cm
∴ Image 10 cm in front of the lens: virtual, erect, 2 cm tall
questions.ans: (a) v = −10 cm (10 cm from the lens, on the object's side) · (b) m = +1/3, h′ = 2 cm: virtual, erect, diminished
questions.remember: A concave lens ALWAYS gives a virtual, erect, diminished image between F and the lens, whatever the object distance.
questions.trap: Using f = +15 for a concave lens. Concave (diverging) lens: f is NEGATIVE.
questions.tryit: What is the power of this lens?

questions.title: Convex lens as a magnifier
questions.text:
(a) Write the expression for the magnification produced by a lens in terms of object distance and image distance.
(b) A 4 cm tall object is placed perpendicular to the principal axis of a convex lens of focal length 20 cm. Calculate the size of the image if the object is 10 cm from the lens.
steps: ② (b) u = −10 cm, f = +20 cm, h = 4 cm
questions.ans: (a) m = h′/h = v/u · (b) v = −20 cm, m = +2, image height 8 cm (virtual, erect, magnified)
questions.remember: Lens: m = v/u. Mirror: m = −v/u. Positive m ⟹ virtual and erect.
questions.trap: Using the mirror formula m = −v/u for a lens: you'd get −2 and a wrong 'inverted' image.
questions.tryit: Where must the object be to get the image at infinity?
questions.tryans: At the focus, 20 cm from the lens

questions.title: The rear-view mirror
steps: ① Rear-view mirror = convex ⟹ f = +2.0 m; u = −8.0 m
④ Positive v ⟹ behind the mirror: virtual, erect
∴ 1.6 m behind the mirror: virtual, erect, smaller
questions.ans: v = +1.6 m: the image is 1.6 m behind the mirror; virtual, erect and diminished (m = +0.2)
questions.remember: Convex mirrors (rear-view mirrors) always give virtual, erect, diminished images and a WIDER field of view.
questions.trap: Taking f = −2 m. A rear-view mirror is CONVEX: f is positive.
questions.tryit: Why are convex mirrors preferred as rear-view mirrors?
questions.tryans: They give an erect image and a much wider field of view
